chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The Qunut in the Witr prayer is seeking forgiveness (Istighfar), and in the obligatory prayer is supplication (Du'a)."

key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: Witr (the odd-numbered prayer performed after Isha)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qunut in Witr and Qunut in obligatory prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the specific spiritual intent behind the Qunut in different prayer contexts, prescribing Istighfar (seeking forgiveness) for the Witr prayer to emphasize repentance and Du'a (general supplication) for obligatory prayers to seek divine aid. This distinction reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on tailoring supplicatory acts to the unique spiritual atmosphere of each prayer type, a view supported by prominent scholars like Al-Kulayni and Al-Tusi in their compilation of hadith. The ruling underscores the importance of mindful devotion (khushu') and the prophetic tradition of varying supplications according to the specific needs of the worshipper during different stages of prayer.
